title: Shared definitions for causeway tool schemas
description: Every tool file's outputSchema describes ONLY the `data` payload. The response envelope { ok, evidenceId, data | unknown } is universal and enforced by modules/mcpserver — never restate it per tool. A tool's x-causeway.unknownReasons lists the reasons it may legitimately return; the server rejects any other.

commitId.description: Full 40-hex commit SHA. Abbreviated SHAs are rejected — ambiguity is not resolvable downstream.

noteId.description: Deliberately NOT an evidenceId. findings.record requires ^ev_, so a note can never be cited as support for a claim. Notes influence what an agent DOES; evidence determines what an agent may SAY.

noteKind.description: Closed set, and deliberately excludes anything claim-shaped. ENVIRONMENT: how this repo builds, what it needs. CONVENTION: how this project words commits, links issues, names tests. DEAD_END: an approach that failed and why, so budget is not spent twice. FIXTURE: setup a harness needs. There is no FACT or FINDING kind — assertions about bugs go through findings.record with evidence, never here.

oldLines.description: Line range in PARENT-commit coordinates. The fault lives here.

newLines.description: Line range in FIX-commit coordinates. The repair lives here.

oldPath.description: Present when the file was renamed.

unknownReason.description: Closed set. A tool needing a reason not listed here must add the case to UnknownReason in modules/core first — never improvise a string. NOTE: every tool declares NotApplicable and ToolUnavailable. Both are universally true: any handler can be asked about a handle, commit or argument that does not resolve (NotApplicable), and any handler can find its backing service — Docker, Neo4j, GitHub — unreachable (ToolUnavailable). Both are determinable-but-absent answers, not failures, and both are citable.
